mainTopic: Actions that can lead to קרי; examination cloths and when blood found on them makes a woman definitely or doubtfully a נדה
overview: The amud begins by finishing אביי's ruling that camel riders may not eat תרומה, because riding can lead to קרי. A ברייתא supports this, and the גמרא gives two explanations of why some donkey drivers are צדיקים and some are רשעים. רבי יהושע בן לוי curses anyone who sleeps flat on his back. The גמרא explains that tilting slightly is enough for sleeping but not for קריאת שמע, except for a heavy person like רבי יוחנן. A new משנה then describes how women check with cloths at relations, and when blood found on them brings definite impurity and a קרבן, or only impurity because of doubt. רבי עקיבא and the חכמים argue whether the husband becomes impure in the doubtful case. The גמרא asks why we don't worry that the blood came from a louse, and gives two versions of רבי זירא's answer, each with a different practical result. Finally it discusses a woman who checked herself and found blood the next day. With a cloth known to be clean, רב, שמואל and the בית מדרש rule she is definitely a נדה. With an unchecked cloth, רבי חייא changed his ruling, and the גמרא begins to clarify what that change was. That clarification continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Camel riders may not eat תרומה
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that camel riders may not eat תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Camel riders are forbidden to eat תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes אביי's ruling that people who ride camels may not eat תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Riding a camel causes rubbing that can lead to קרי. Someone who had קרי is טמא and may not eat תרומה. So אביי assumes camel riders are often in that state.

keyTerms.meaning: The holy portion given to a כהן, eaten only in טהרה

phrases.english: Camel riders are forbidden
to eat תרומה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends a statement of אביי that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Camel riders may not eat תרומה because they may have had קרי.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports אביי: camel riders, sailors, and donkey drivers
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says camel riders are all רשעים, sailors are all צדיקים, and donkey drivers are mixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: Camel riders are all wicked, sailors are all righteous, and donkey drivers are some wicked and some righteous.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports אביי's view about camel riders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא calls camel riders רשעים, which fits אביי's worry that riding leads to קרי. Sailors are called צדיקים, because their dangerous work keeps their hearts turned to ה׳ in prayer. Donkey drivers are mixed, and the next steps explain why.

keyTerms.meaning: "Also so": a source teaches the same idea

phrases.english: It is also taught so in a ברייתא:
Camel riders are all wicked,
sailors are all righteous,
donkey drivers: some of them are wicked
and some of them are righteous.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's ruling from step 1.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's ruling that camel riders are suspected of קרי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא calling all camel riders רשעים

steps.title: First explanation: a saddled or unsaddled donkey
steps.stepSummary: One opinion says the difference between donkey drivers is whether the donkey has a saddle.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: this one has a saddle, and that one has no saddle.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why some donkey drivers are צדיקים and some are רשעים. The first view says it depends on the saddle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rider on a saddled donkey does not rub directly against the animal, so there is no worry of קרי. A rider on a bare donkey does rub against it, so he is like the camel rider.

phrases.english: There are those who say:
this is one who is saddled, that is one who is not saddled;
phrases.notes: The righteous one rides a saddled donkey; the wicked one rides a bare donkey.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי הָא דְּמִכַּף הָא דְּלָא מִכַּף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the mixed ruling on donkey drivers in step 2.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is whether the donkey is saddled.

steps.title: Second explanation: how the rider sits
steps.stepSummary: A second opinion says the difference is whether the rider spreads his legs on both sides of the donkey.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: this one spreads his legs, and that one does not spread his legs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different explanation of the donkey drivers: it depends on how the rider sits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A rider who sits with one leg on each side of the donkey rubs against it, so he is the רשע. A rider who sits with both legs on one side does not rub, so he is the צדיק.

keyTerms.meaning: Spreads his legs on both sides of the animal

phrases.english: And there are those who say:
this is one who spreads his legs, that is one who does not spread his legs.
phrases.notes: Here the one who spreads his legs is the wicked one, and the one who sits sideways is the righteous one.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיכָּא דְאָמְרִי הָא דִּמְטַרְטֵין הָא דְּלָא מְטַרְטֵין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second explanation, instead of the saddle explanation in step 3.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is whether the rider spreads his legs on both sides.
steps.whatToRemember: The donkey drivers are mixed. One view says it depends on the saddle; the other says it depends on how the rider sits.

steps.title: רבי יהושע בן לוי curses one who sleeps on his back
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי would curse anyone who sleeps lying flat on his back.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי would curse one who sleeps on his back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to another action that can lead to קרי: sleeping flat on one's back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי held this was serious enough to deserve a curse, because sleeping face-up can lead to קרי. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi
would curse one who sleeps lying on his back.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לָיֵיט אַמַּאן דְּגָנֵי אַפַּרְקִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic on the same theme of avoiding קרי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sleeping flat on one's back is strongly forbidden.

steps.title: Challenge from רב יוסף: only קריאת שמע is forbidden on one's back
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף only forbids saying קריאת שמע on one's back, which suggests that sleeping that way is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that so? But רב יוסף said: One lying on his back may not recite קריאת שמע. That means only קריאת שמע he may not recite, but sleeping that way is fine!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יהושע בן לוי, using a statement of רב יוסף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף only mentions קריאת שמע as forbidden while lying face-up. From his silence, the גמרא infers that just sleeping that way is allowed. That contradicts רבי יהושע בן לוי's curse.

phrases.english: Is that so? But didn't Rav Yosef say:
one lying on his back may not recite "קריאת שמע"
it is קריאת שמע that he may not recite,
but sleeping that way is fine!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע בן לוי's curse on sleeping face-up
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יוסף forbids only קריאת שמע on one's back, which implies sleeping that way is permitted.

steps.title: Answer: tilting slightly helps for sleeping but not for קריאת שמע
steps.stepSummary: Lying on one's back while tilted a little to the side is fine for sleeping, but still forbidden for קריאת שמע.
steps.simpleTranslation: For sleeping, when he tilts slightly to the side, it is fine. For קריאת שמע, even when he tilts slightly, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction by talking about someone who is tilted a little to the side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף was speaking about someone slightly tilted. For sleeping, a small tilt is enough to avoid the danger, so it is allowed. For קריאת שמע, a small tilt is still not respectful enough, so it is forbidden. רבי יהושע בן לוי's curse is about lying fully flat.
steps.confusionAlert: Here מַצְלֵי does not mean "praying". It means leaning or tilting slightly to the side.

phrases.aramaic: לְעִנְיַן מִגְנָא, כִּי מַצְלֵי — שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי.
phrases.english: Regarding sleeping, when he tilts slightly, it is fine.

phrases.aramaic: לְעִנְיַן קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע, כִּי מַצְלֵי — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: Regarding קריאת שמע, even when he tilts slightly, it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעִנְיַן מִגְנָא כִּי מַצְלֵי שַׁפִּיר דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different case: one fully flat versus one slightly tilted
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף's statement suggests sleeping fully on one's back is allowed.
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יוסף is talking about one slightly tilted. That is fine for sleeping but not for קריאת שמע. Lying fully flat is still cursed.

steps.title: Challenge: רבי יוחנן said קריאת שמע while tilted
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן used to tilt slightly and say קריאת שמע, which seems to contradict the answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: But רבי יוחנן would tilt slightly and recite קריאת שמע!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer by pointing to what רבי יוחנן used to do.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer just said that saying קריאת שמע while only slightly tilted is forbidden. Yet רבי יוחנן did exactly that, so it seems to be allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: "But surely": introduces a challenge from a fact

phrases.english: But Rabbi Yoḥanan would tilt slightly
and recite קריאת שמע!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מַצְלֵי וְקָרֵי קְרִיאַת שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that קריאת שמע is forbidden even when slightly tilted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's own practice was to say קריאת שמע while slightly tilted.

steps.title: Answer: רבי יוחנן was heavy
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן was different because he was heavy and could not turn further onto his side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן is different, because he was heavy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן's case was special, so it does not prove anything for everyone else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because רבי יוחנן was heavy, a slight tilt was as far as he could turn. For him that counted as enough. The general rule from step 7 stays in place.
steps.whatToRemember: Sleeping fully flat on one's back is cursed. Tilting slightly is fine for sleeping, but not for קריאת שמע, except for someone heavy like רבי יוחנן who cannot turn more.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan is different,
since he was heavy.
phrases.notes: Because he was heavy, a slight tilt was as far as he could turn.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן דְּבַעַל בָּשָׂר הֲוָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's practice shows a slight tilt is enough for קריאת שמע.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only someone heavy, who cannot turn more, may rely on a slight tilt for קריאת שמע.

steps.title: The custom of using examination cloths
steps.stepSummary: Jewish women use two examination cloths at relations, one for the husband and one for the wife. Modest women prepare a third cloth to check themselves beforehand.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Jewish women have relations using two examination cloths, one for him and one for her. Modest women prepare a third cloth to check themselves before.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens by describing a common practice: checking with cloths so that any blood is noticed. This sets up the rulings that follow about what happens when blood is found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two cloths are used after relations: his cloth shows if her blood is on him, and hers shows if her period began. The third cloth, used by modest women, is a check before relations, so they start off sure they are clean.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'witnesses': examination cloths that show whether there is blood

phrases.english: MISHNA
The custom of Jewish women
is to have relations using two examination cloths
phrases.notes: עדים usually means 'witnesses.' Here they are cloths that 'testify' whether there is blood.

phrases.english: one for him and one for her
and the modest women prepare a third
to prepare 'the house'
phrases.notes: 'The house' is a polite way of referring to her private area. She checks it before relations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה begins, unrelated to the previous discussion about sleeping positions.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The normal practice is to use two examination cloths, and modest women add a third one for a check beforehand.

steps.title: Three cases of blood found on the cloths
steps.stepSummary: Blood on his cloth, or on hers right away: both are טמא and owe a קרבן. Blood on hers after some time: both are טמא because of the doubt, but they owe no קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If blood is found on his cloth, they are impure and must bring a קרבן. If it is found on hers right away, they are impure and must bring a קרבן. If it is found on hers after some time, they are impure because of the doubt, and they do not bring a קרבן.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives the rulings for three different findings on the cloths.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Blood on his cloth, or on hers right away, proves she was a נדה during relations. So both are טמא, and each must bring a קרבן חטאת for doing a כרת sin by mistake. If the blood shows up only after a delay, maybe it came after relations. That doubt makes them טמא but frees them from the קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Ritually impure (here, the seven-day impurity of נדה)
An offering; here the חטאת brought for an accidental sin

steps.confusionAlert: 'Exempt from the קרבן' does not mean they are pure. They are still טמא; only the offering is not required, because it is not clear they sinned.

phrases.english: If blood was found on his cloth
they are impure and liable to bring an offering
If it was found on hers immediately
they are impure and liable to bring an offering
If it was found on hers after some time
they are impure because of the doubt
and they are exempt from the offering

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצָא עַל שֶׁלּוֹ טְמֵאִין וְחַיָּיבִין קׇרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the rulings for what the cloths described in step 10 might show.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Certain blood during relations means impurity plus a קרבן. Blood found after a delay means impurity because of doubt, with no קרבן.

steps.title: What counts as 'after some time'?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה asks how long a delay counts as 'after some time.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'after some time'?
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה stops to define its own term. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference between 'right away' and 'after some time' decides whether a קרבן is owed. So the משנה needs a clear measure of time.

keyTerms.meaning: Which is it? What counts as

phrases.english: What is considered 'after some time'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of a phrase used in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How much delay turns a finding into the doubtful 'after some time' case.

steps.title: Long enough to get down and wash
steps.stepSummary: 'After some time' means the time it takes her to get off the bed and wash herself.
steps.simpleTranslation: Enough time for her to get down from the bed and wash her face.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה answers its own question with a practical measure of time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the check comes within that short span, the blood counts as present during relations. If it comes later, the blood may have appeared only afterward, so the case becomes a ספק.

phrases.english: Enough time for her to get down from the bed
and rinse her face
phrases.notes: 'Her face' is a polite way of saying her private area.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּדֵי שֶׁתֵּרֵד מִן הַמִּטָּה וְתָדִיחַ פָּנֶיהָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'After some time' is the time it takes her to get off the bed and wash.

steps.title: In the delayed case: she is impure backward 24 hours, but her husband is not
steps.stepSummary: When blood is found after that delay, she makes things impure going back 24 hours, but she does not pass the impurity of a נדה to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: And after that time, she makes things impure going back twenty-four hours, but she does not make the man who had relations with her impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה (the view of the תנא קמא) gives the detailed result of the 'after some time' case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since we cannot tell exactly when the blood started, items she touched in the last 24 hours become impure, a rule of the חכמים. But her husband does not get the seven-day impurity of someone who had relations with a נדה. That impurity is reserved for when she is known to have been a נדה during relations.

keyTerms.meaning: From time to time: the full 24 hours going backward
The man who had relations with her

phrases.english: And after that, she makes things impure for the past twenty-four hours
but she does not make the man who had relations with her impure
phrases.notes: He means the seven-day impurity of being with a נדה. That is what she does not pass on to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out what the impurity 'because of doubt' from step 11 means in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the delayed case, she is impure backward for 24 hours, but her husband does not get the seven-day impurity.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: the husband is impure too
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא disagrees and says that in the delayed case she also makes her husband impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא says: She even makes the man who had relations with her impure.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא argues with the view just stated about the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree she goes back 24 hours. They argue only about the husband. Since her impurity reaches back over the time of relations, רבי עקיבא gives the husband the seven-day impurity as well, a rule of the חכמים.

keyTerms.meaning: The first, unnamed opinion in the משנה

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva says
she even makes the man who had relations with her impure

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר אַף מְטַמְּאָה אֶת בּוֹעֲלָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the last part of step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the delayed case, the husband also gets the seven-day impurity.

steps.title: The חכמים agree with רבי עקיבא about a woman who saw a stain
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים agree that a woman who saw a כתם makes the man who has relations with her impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים agree with רבי עקיבא that a woman who sees a stain makes the man who has relations with her impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes by noting one case where the חכמים agree with רבי עקיבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a כתם, she already saw the stain before relations, so she was impure going in. In that case even the חכמים say her husband gets the seven-day impurity, which is also a rule of the חכמים. Their argument is limited to blood found after the delay.

keyTerms.meaning: A blood stain found on a garment or body, not felt coming out

steps.whatToRemember: Certain blood during relations means impurity plus a קרבן. Doubtful, delayed blood means impurity only, and they argue whether the husband is affected. A known כתם before relations makes the husband impure according to everyone.

phrases.english: The Sages agree with Rabbi Akiva
about a woman who sees a stain
that she makes the man who has relations with her impure

steps.triggerLanguage: מוֹדִים חֲכָמִים לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּרוֹאָה כֶּתֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the disagreement of steps 14 and 15 by naming a case where everyone agrees.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Everyone agrees that a woman who saw a כתם makes the man who has relations with her impure. The argument is only about blood found after the delay.

steps.title: Maybe the blood came from a louse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling that blood found on the husband's cloth makes both of them definitely impure. Perhaps it came from a crushed louse.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Shouldn't we worry that maybe it is the blood of a louse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion by challenging the משנה. Why are we sure the blood is hers? Maybe a louse was crushed during relations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treated the blood as definite proof that she is a נדה. If a louse could be the source, the impurity should only be a doubt. The question goes after how certain the משנה's ruling really is.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
Let us be concerned about a possibility
Blood of a louse (a small insect)

phrases.english: Gemara:
But let us be concerned that perhaps
it is the blood of a louse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's ruling that both are definitely impure
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that blood found on the husband's cloth makes both of them definitely impure and liable to a קרבן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Another possible source of the blood, a louse, should turn the impurity into a doubt

steps.title: The area is checked and has no lice
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא answers that this place is considered 'checked' and is known to be free of lice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: That place is checked with regard to a louse.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא answers the challenge. Lice are not found in that area at all, so the blood must be hers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בָּדוּק means the place is already 'known clean' of lice. So there is no real chance the blood came from a louse, and the משנה's certainty stands.

keyTerms.meaning: That place (a polite way of saying her private area)
Checked, known to be free of something

phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira says:
That place is examined
with regard to a louse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the louse challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Factual rejection of the alternative source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A louse might have been crushed there
steps.terutzMaskana: Lice are not found in that place, so the blood is hers

steps.title: Second version: The area is too narrow for a louse
steps.stepSummary: Another version of רבי זירא's answer says the place is too narrow for a louse.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: It is too narrow for a louse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of רבי זירא's answer. A louse can't easily get into that area because it is too tight.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions reach the same result: we don't worry about a louse. But the reason is different. One says lice are never there, and the other says lice usually can't get in.

phrases.english: And some say:
It is narrow with regard to a louse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the answer in step 18
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A louse might have been crushed there
steps.terutzMaskana: A louse normally cannot get into so narrow a place

steps.title: What is the difference between the two versions?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference there is between 'checked' and 'narrow.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the difference between them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether the two versions ever lead to a different result. It is setting up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions say not to worry about a louse. So the גמרא wants a case where the two reasons would give different rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the practical difference between them?

phrases.english: What is the difference between them?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Compares the two versions from steps 18 and 19
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A case where the two versions of רבי זירא give different results

steps.title: The difference: A crushed louse was found
steps.stepSummary: The difference comes up when a crushed louse is actually found. 'Checked' says it came from elsewhere. 'Narrow' says maybe the man crushed it during relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: The difference is where a crushed louse was found. According to 'checked,' it came from somewhere else. According to 'narrow,' say the man's organ crushed it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the difference shows up when a crushed louse is found on the cloth. The two versions then rule differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the place is 'checked,' a louse is never there, so a crushed louse must have come from elsewhere and the blood is still hers. She is definitely impure. If the place is only 'narrow,' a louse could rarely get in, so the blood might be the louse's and the impurity is a doubt.
steps.whatToRemember: בָּדוּק = lice are never there, so she is impure even if a crushed louse is found. דָּחוּק = lice rarely get there, so a crushed louse makes it a doubt.

phrases.english: There is a difference between them
where a crushed louse was found.
According to this version, which says 'it is examined' —
this one came from elsewhere,
according to that version, which says 'it is narrow' —
say the organ crushed it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 20
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: When a crushed louse is found: according to 'checked' she is impure, and according to 'narrow' the impurity is a doubt

steps.title: רב: Blood found on a checked cloth next day makes her a definite נדה
steps.stepSummary: A woman checked herself with a cloth she knew was clean and pressed it against her thigh. The next day she found blood on it. רב rules she is definitely a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: She checked with a cloth that she had checked, pressed it against her thigh, and the next day found blood on it. רב said: She is impure as a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case. רב rules that the blood counts as definite proof that she is a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The cloth was known to be clean before she used it. So the blood found later must have come from her check. רב treats this as certain, not as a doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: A cloth already checked and known to be clean

phrases.english: It was stated:
She examined herself with a cloth that had been examined by her,
and she pressed it against her thigh,
phrases.notes: She did not look at the cloth after checking. She just put it against her thigh.

phrases.english: and the next day she found blood on it.
Rav says: She is impure as a menstruating woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new case about a check cloth
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blood found the next day on a cloth that was clean before the check makes her definitely a נדה

steps.title: רב שימי: But you told us 'she is concerned'
steps.stepSummary: רב שימי בר חייא challenges רב. Earlier רב said she only 'needs to be concerned,' which sounds like a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שימי בר חייא said to him: But you told us 'she is concerned'!
steps.whatsHappening: רב שימי בר חייא points out that רב seems to contradict himself. Earlier רב called this a case of doubt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word חוֹשֶׁשֶׁת means a worry, a doubtful impurity. That clashes with רב's new ruling that she is definitely a נדה. The גמרא does not answer רב שימי directly. Instead, the next steps bring שמואל and the ruling of the בית מדרש, which back the 'definite' ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: She must be concerned, meaning a doubtful impurity

steps.confusionAlert: חוֹשֶׁשֶׁת is not the same as טְמֵאָה נִדָּה. One means 'maybe impure,' the other means 'definitely impure.'

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שִׁימִי בַּר חִיָּיא:
phrases.english: Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya said to him:
But you said to us 'she is concerned'!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's ruling in step 22
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling of definite נדה impurity
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב earlier taught that this is only a doubt (חוששת)

steps.title: שמואל also rules she is a definite נדה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings שמואל, who rules the same way as רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also stated: שמואל said: She is impure as a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports רב's ruling by showing that שמואל said the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב שימי's challenge pointed toward a doubt. Now we see שמואל also holds she is definitely a נדה. This gives the ruling of 'definite' more weight.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also stated: brings support from another sage

phrases.english: It was also stated:
Shmuel says: She is impure as a menstruating woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב's ruling against the challenge
steps.raayaObject: רב's ruling that she is definitely a נדה

steps.title: The בית מדרש rules she is a definite נדה
steps.stepSummary: The practice in the בית מדרש is to rule that she is definitely a נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so they rule in the בית מדרש: She is impure as a נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא ends this case with the practical ruling of the בית מדרש: she is definitely a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This settles the הלכה in practice. It goes like רב's ruling and שמואל's, not like 'חוששת.'
steps.whatToRemember: A woman who checked with a clean cloth and found blood on it the next day is definitely a נדה. This is the ruling of רב, שמואל, and the בית מדרש.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical הלכה for this case.

phrases.english: And so they rule in the study hall:
She is impure as a menstruating woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the final practical ruling after שמואל's support
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In practice she is definitely a נדה

steps.title: Unchecked cloth found with blood the next day: רבי חייא changed his ruling
steps.stepSummary: A woman checked herself with a cloth she had not checked first. She put it in a box and found blood on it the next day. רב יוסף reports that רבי חייא ruled her impure for most of his life, but ruled her pure in his old age.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: A woman checked herself with a cloth she had not checked beforehand. She put it in a box, and the next day she found blood on it. רב יוסף said: All his days רבי חייא ruled her impure, but in his old age he ruled her pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case that is like the one before, but with one change: this time the cloth was not checked before she used it. רב יוסף tells us that רבי חייא changed his mind about this case over his lifetime.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22 the cloth was known to be clean, so the blood clearly came from her body. Here the cloth was not checked, so the blood may have been on it before the check. That doubt is why רבי חייא could move toward a more lenient ruling later in life.

keyTerms.meaning: A checking cloth a woman uses to examine herself
He ruled impure / he ruled pure

phrases.aramaic: אִתְּמַר: בָּדְקָה בְּעֵד שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּדוּק לָהּ,
phrases.english: It was stated: She examined herself with a cloth that had not been checked by her,
and she put it in a box,
and the next day she found blood on it.
Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל יָמָיו שֶׁל רַבִּי חִיָּיא טִימֵּא,
phrases.english: All the days of Rabbi Ḥiyya, he ruled her impure,
but in his old age he ruled her pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: בָּדְקָה בְּעֵד שֶׁאֵינוֹ בָּדוּק לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a cloth known to be clean (steps 22-25) to a cloth that was never checked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא first ruled such a woman impure, and in his old age ruled her pure.

steps.title: What exactly did רבי חייא change?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב יוסף meant. Maybe רבי חייא first said definite נדה and later said only כתם. Or maybe he first said כתם and later said fully pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: What does he mean? Option one: all his days he ruled her impure as a נדה, and in his old age he ruled she is not a נדה but is still impure because of a כתם. Or option two: all his days he ruled her impure because of a כתם, and in his old age he ruled her completely pure?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רב יוסף's report, since 'impure' and 'pure' can each mean two different things here. It lays out two possible readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being impure 'as a נדה' is a definite impurity. Impure 'because of a כתם' (a stain) is a lighter, doubtful impurity. So the change could be one step down, either from definite to doubtful, or from doubtful to nothing at all.

keyTerms.meaning: How does he mean it? What is he saying?
Because of being a נדה: a definite impurity
A stain: blood found that may not come from a true flow, which is a doubtful impurity
Or perhaps: introduces the other side of the question
From anything at all: completely pure

steps.confusionAlert: Both readings agree that רבי חייא became more lenient. The only question is where he started and where he ended up: נדה to כתם, or כתם to pure.

phrases.english: It was asked of them: How does he mean it?
All his days he ruled her impure as a menstruating woman,
and in his old age he ruled her pure from being a menstruating woman,
but ruled her impure because of a stain.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ דִלְמָא: כׇּל יָמָיו טִימֵּא מִשּׁוּם כֶּתֶם,
phrases.english: Or perhaps: all his days he ruled her impure because of a stain,
and in his old age he ruled her pure from any impurity at all?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the words 'impure' and 'pure' in רב יוסף's report actually mean.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Did רבי חייא's ruling move from נדה to כתם, or from כתם to completely pure?

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי says נדה, רבי חייא says כתם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the same case. רבי rules she is impure as a נדה. רבי חייא rules she is impure because of a כתם.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for it was taught: A woman checked herself with a cloth she had not checked beforehand, put it in a box, and the next day found blood on it. רבי says: She is impure as a נדה. רבי חייא says: She is impure because of a כתם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to try to answer the question from step 27. In it, רבי חייא is recorded as holding 'impure because of a כתם.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows that at some point רבי חייא held the middle position, כתם. The גמרא will use this to figure out which of the two readings of רב יוסף fits. The full answer comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: She is impure as a נדה: definite impurity
She is impure because of a stain: doubtful impurity

phrases.english: Come and hear, as it is taught:
She examined herself with a cloth that had not been checked by her,
and she put it in a box,
and the next day she found blood on it,
Rabbi says: She is impure as a menstruating woman,
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no other name means רבי יהודה הנשיא, the one who put together the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי חִיָּיא אָמַר: טְמֵאָה מִשּׁוּם כֶּתֶם.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Ḥiyya says: She is impure because of a stain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to try to settle the question of step 27.
steps.raayaObject: Which reading of רב יוסף's report about רבי חייא is correct
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי rules נדה and רבי חייא rules כתם in this exact case
